The complete 3,324-byte capture had observed SHA-256 9d6b43ce4d8de0c878bf16b54d8e7a10d9bd42b75178153e3af6a815bdc90f74, matching the claim's provenance. The connector measured SHA-256 25b5911740d53cd648267246d1bdafe9d9c053a4ff7dde791e37108d6def395b for [248,580). The separately fetched claim record at ab83a4adb7ae90d20dbf15e22ccc4ed2e2645902 matched the requested record digest. challenge.method: Tested the repository-wide reading and the sufficiency of a GPL grant by comparing the same-release iostream notice [0,1200) with the libcc1.cc header [0,710). Checked the reference to separate terms against GPLv3 section 7, then read exception section 1 to test whether file eligibility alone decides conveyance.
challenge.results: The iostream notice names GPLv3 section 7 and grants the additional permissions described in exception version 3.1, pointing to COPYING3 and COPYING.RUNTIME for the terms. The visible libcc1.cc header grants GPL version 3 or later and points to COPYING3, with no exception notice in the inspected range. The difference accords with the publisher's file-specific condition. Section 1 separately requires a Target Code combination with Independent Modules, generation of all Target Code by Eligible Compilation Processes, and conveyance terms consistent with the licensing of the Independent Modules. File eligibility alone therefore leaves the conveyance question open.

limitations: The assessment covers the stated file-level condition for exception version 3.1 under GPLv3. Repository-wide grants, future GPL editions, and canonical graph relationships are outside that scope.
The compiler comparison is limited to the visible header. Its silence about the exception does not determine the file's complete legal status.
A specific conveyance requires separate assessment of the Target Code, the compilation processes, and the Independent Modules.
reasoning:
The opening applicability paragraph in the declared range reads:

This GCC Runtime Library Exception ("Exception") is an additional
permission under section 7 of the GNU General Public License, version
3 ("GPLv3"). It applies to a given file (the "Runtime Library") that
bears a notice placed by the copyright holder of the file stating that
the file is governed by GPLv3 along with this Exception.

The GPLv3 section 7 excerpts [17791,18760) and [20624,21034) explain that additional permissions can apply to part of a program and that a relevant source file may carry a notice indicating where to find the applicable terms.
